name: Santo Data Centre (Australia-funded, Nakamal Agreement)
developer: Government of Vanuatu (funded by Australian Government)
notes: Second of two data centres funded by Australia (combined value A$120m/US$79m) under the Nakamal Agreement, located on the island of Santo (Espiritu Santo, Sanma province). Vanuatu government announced the pair in 2024 as part of an e-commerce/digital economy strategy; agreement initialled 13 Aug 2025 and signed 29 Jun 2026. Details sparse; no public MW capacity.

name: Vanuatu Government Datacenter
notes: Government data centre in Port Vila near the Meteo Department Building, housing nine racks with a second smaller data centre for redundancy; hosts the Vanuatu Internet Exchange (VIX.VU, 6 networks per PeeringDB) and connects to the submarine cable landing station with direct access to an Equinix data centre in Sydney (per DataCenterDynamics, Aug 2025). PeeringDB facility record 2080 updated 2025-09-26. No public MW capacity.

name: Interchange Port Vila Cable Station Data Centre (ICX)
notes: Archived official Interchange project page (2013) lists new data centre facilities with 22 racks incorporated within the Port Vila cable station of the ICX submarine cable system (Port Vila-Suva, linking to Southern Cross), including co-location facilities for customers; cable ready for service Jan 2014. Still referenced as the Vanuatu landing station/colo point. No public MW capacity.

name: Vanuatu Data Park
notes: Small local data centre/web hosting service; primary evidence is a YouTube channel titled 'Vanuatu Data Centre and web hosting'. Location (likely Port Vila) and scale unverified; no public MW capacity.

name: Port Vila Data Centre (Australia-funded, Nakamal Agreement)
developer: Government of Vanuatu (funded by Australian Government)
notes: One of two data centres (combined value A$120m/US$79m) announced by Vanuatu's government in 2024 for its e-commerce/digital economy strategy and funded by Australia under the Nakamal Agreement (initialled 13 Aug 2025; signed 29 Jun 2026). Located in the capital Port Vila. Details sparse; no public MW capacity.
